svg.font-family: Amazon Ember, Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Microservices platform (AppStack) architecture on AWS. 1. Users load the admin SPA from a private S3 bucket through CloudFront (OAC). 2. Users reach the Application Load Balancer on HTTPS 443; it forwards HTTP to the ECS hosts. 3. The microservices use RDS PostgreSQL (5432), ElastiCache Redis (6379) and OpenSearch (443). 4. The microservices publish to SQS price-sync. 5. PDFs uploaded to the ingest bucket send ObjectCreated events to SQS pdf-sync. 6. The workers consume both queues, batch-insert into RDS and update the OpenSearch index. 7. The EC2 container hosts pull images from ECR. 8. GitHub Actions assumes the OIDC roles; terraform apply holds the DynamoDB state lock. Private subnets (1a / 1b) have no internet route: S3 and DynamoDB gateway endpoints replace a NAT gateway.
svg.text: CI/CD via OIDC, no static keys
Users load the admin SPA from a private S3 bucket through CloudFront (OAC).
Users reach the Application Load Balancer on HTTPS 443; it forwards HTTP to the ECS hosts.
The microservices use RDS PostgreSQL (5432), ElastiCache Redis (6379) and OpenSearch (443).
The microservices publish to SQS price-sync.
PDFs uploaded to the ingest bucket send ObjectCreated events to SQS pdf-sync.
The workers consume both queues, batch-insert into RDS and update the OpenSearch index.
The EC2 container hosts pull images from ECR.
GitHub Actions assumes the OIDC roles; terraform apply holds the DynamoDB state lock.
Dashed lines follow the source diagram: the workers' batch insert and terraform apply.
Private subnets (1a / 1b) have no internet route: S3 and DynamoDB gateway endpoints replace a NAT gateway.
